sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上奇妙有趣的知识，同时提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the history of mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将聊聊雇佣兵的历史。

sentences.en: It is a fascinating story, and will take us from the Italian Renaissance to the Iraq War to modern-day Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引人入胜的故事，将带我们从意大利文艺复兴时期走到伊拉克战争，再到当今的乌克兰。

sentences.en: We will explore how the nature of mercenaries has evolved over time, the changing reasons to use or not to use mercenary forces, and what this means for the grim business of warfare in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨雇佣兵的本质是如何随时间演变的，使用或不使用雇佣兵的原因发生了怎样的变化，以及这对21世纪残酷的战争生意意味着什么。

sentences.en: Alright then, let’s get cracking and talk about the history of mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们切入正题，聊聊雇佣兵的历史。

sentences.en: In 2016 Forbes Magazine published an article titled “The Rise of the Freelancer Economy”.
sentences.zh: 2016年，《福布斯》杂志发表了一篇题为《自由职业者经济的崛起》的文章。

sentences.en: In it, the author wrote, and I’m quoting directly, “Who says you can’t drive an Uber in the morning, design websites all afternoon, and cater your own food company at night?”
sentences.zh: 文章中，作者写道——我直接引述：“谁说你不能早上开优步，下午设计网站，晚上经营自己的餐饮公司呢？”

sentences.en: He went on to claim that by the year 2020, 50% of the US workforce would be freelance.
sentences.zh: 他接着声称，到2020年，美国50%的劳动力将是自由职业者。

sentences.en: Now, this hasn’t happened, the true number is around 38%.
sentences.zh: 然而，这并没有发生，真实的数据大约是38%。

sentences.en: And in fact, the idea of this being “new” or “on the rise” is also somewhat problematic.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种认为这是“新鲜事物”或“正在崛起”的观点也有点问题。

sentences.en: Even the word “freelance” in English gives us a clue about the age of the idea of not being tied to one boss or master.
sentences.zh: 甚至英语中的“freelance”（自由职业）一词也为我们提供了一个线索，说明不绑定于某个老板或主人的这种观念有多久远。

sentences.en: It was coined in the early 19th century but to refer to European knights in the Medieval Era who were not ideologically or politically aligned with any one ruler and who would fight for money.
sentences.zh: 它创造于19世纪初，但指的是中世纪时期的欧洲骑士，他们在意识形态或政治上不效忠于任何一个统治者，而是为钱而战。

sentences.en: They often carried lances, which are the long pointy spears that they would hold out in front of their galloping horses, and these lances were free, or at least freely available to the highest bidder, the person who was prepared to pay the most money.
sentences.zh: 他们通常携带骑枪，也就是他们骑着飞奔的马匹时向前平举的长尖矛，这些骑枪是自由的，或者至少是可以自由提供给最高出价者——也就是准备付最多钱的人。

sentences.en: These “freelancers” are what we might today call “mercenaries”, professional soldiers who fight on behalf of whoever will pay.
sentences.zh: 这些“自由枪骑兵”（freelancers）就是我们今天可能称之为“雇佣兵”（mercenaries）的人，他们是为出价最高者而战的职业军人。

sentences.en: Now, the term “mercenary” is also a little problematic, and we will come to discuss the different types of mercenaries as we move through the episode.
sentences.zh: 现在，“雇佣兵”这个词也有一点问题，随着节目的推进，我们将来讨论不同类型的雇佣兵。

sentences.en: And, of course, the idea of someone being a mercenary did not start in the medieval era or in Europe.
sentences.zh: 当然，有人作为雇佣兵的想法并不是从中世纪或欧洲开始的。

sentences.en: There is evidence of mercenary fighters all over the world and throughout history: Ancient Persia, Carthage, Qin Dynasty China, and Ancient Egypt.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，雇佣兵在世界各地和整个历史上都存在：古代波斯、迦太基、中国秦朝和古埃及。

sentences.en: It made sense, back then, just as it does in some cases now.
sentences.zh: 这在当时说得通，就像在某些情况下现在依然说得通一样。

sentences.en: Keeping a fully-trained army was and still is a very expensive thing to do, especially for a small state.
sentences.zh: 维持一支训练有素的军队过去是、现在仍然是一件非常昂贵的事情，对于一个小国来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: And before the idea of nationhood that we have today, before this notion of nationality and belonging to a country, it was understandably harder to convince someone to fight and die on a battlefield for…what?
sentences.zh: 而在我们今天所拥有的国家观念出现之前，在拥有国籍和从属于某个国家这种概念之前，可以理解的是，很难说服一个人为了……什么而在战场上战斗并牺牲？

sentences.en: For glory? For loyalty to a ruler they would almost certainly never meet?
sentences.zh: 为了荣誉？为了效忠一个他们几乎肯定永远不会见面的统治者？

sentences.en: The Roman poet Horace famously wrote “Dulce et decorum est pro patria mori” - “It is sweet and right to die for one’s homeland”.
sentences.zh: 罗马诗人贺拉斯有一句名言：“为祖国战死是甜蜜而光荣的”——“Dulce et decorum est pro patria mori”。

sentences.en: This might make for a nice line in a poem, but the reality of convincing someone to risk their life for an abstract ideal like glory or loyalty, especially before the modern idea of nationhood, well, it was difficult.
sentences.zh: 这或许能拼凑出一首好诗，但要说服某人为诸如荣誉或忠诚之类的抽象理想去冒生命危险，特别是在现代国家观念出现之前，现实中，嗯，这很困难。

sentences.en: But how about fighting for money? Money was universal.
sentences.zh: 但是为了钱战斗呢？钱是通用的。

sentences.en: It talked then, just as it talks now. Throughout history there have been people willing to lay their lives on the line, for a fee, of course.
sentences.zh: 它过去说话算数，现在也一样。纵观历史，一直有人愿意为了报酬把生命押在生死线上，当然是有偿的。

sentences.en: Now, to explore the idea of mercenaries, we are going to focus on three particular groups of mercenaries, one, hundreds of years old, another, three decades old, and another where the story is unfortunately still unfolding.
sentences.zh: 现在，为了探讨雇佣兵的概念，我们将聚焦于三类特定的雇佣兵：一组存在于数百年前，另一组诞生于三十年前，还有一组的故事不幸仍在继续。

sentences.en: Our first stop on this mercenary tour is Renaissance Italy.
sentences.zh: 我们这趟雇佣兵之旅的第一站是文艺复兴时期的意大利。

sentences.en: Renaissance Italy was a chaotic place. It was not the unified country we know today, but a collection of city-states—Venice, Florence, Milan, the Papal States, Naples—each one with its own ruler, ambitions, and, often, enemies.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴时期的意大利是一个混乱的地方。它不是我们今天所知道的统一国家，而是一组城邦——威尼斯、佛罗伦萨、米兰、教皇国、那不勒斯——每一个都有自己的统治者、野心，而且通常还有敌人。

sentences.en: These city-states were frequently at war with each other, whether over trade, territory, or sheer political rivalry.
sentences.zh: 这些城邦经常彼此交战，无论是为了贸易、领土，还是纯粹的政治竞争。

sentences.en: But there was one big problem: maintaining a standing army was expensive, and these city-states, wealthy as they were, preferred to spend their money on art, architecture, and trade.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个大问题：维持一支常备军是昂贵的，而这些城邦尽管富有，却更愿意把钱花在艺术、建筑和贸易上。

sentences.en: So, instead of building their own armies, they turned to mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们没有建立自己的军队，而是求助于雇佣兵。

sentences.en: These mercenaries were organised into companies led by people called condottieri.
sentences.zh: 这些雇佣兵被组织成由被称为 condottieri 的人领导的连队。

sentences.en: The word condottieri comes from the Italian word condotta, which means “conduct” or “behaviour” in modern Italian, but in the Renaissance era meant “contract” or “agreement.”
sentences.zh: “condottieri”这个词源于意大利语单词 condotta，在现代意大利语中意为“品行”或“行为”，但在文艺复兴时期意为“合同”或“协议”。

sentences.en: These condottieri were leaders of mercenary bands, hired through a formal contract to fight on behalf of a city-state.
sentences.zh: 这些 condottieri 是雇佣兵团的首领，通过正式合同受雇为某个城邦作战。

sentences.en: They were professional soldiers who would hire out their services to the highest bidder.
sentences.zh: 他们是职业军人，将自己的服务出租给最高出价者。

sentences.en: They didn’t fight for loyalty, honour, or patriotism—they fought for money.
sentences.zh: 他们不为忠诚、荣誉或爱国主义而战——他们为钱而战。

sentences.en: And for the rulers of Renaissance Italy, this arrangement worked well…at least, in theory.
sentences.zh: 对于文艺复兴时期意大利的统治者来说，这种安排运作良好……至少在理论上是这样。

sentences.en: But there was a catch: these condottieri weren’t exactly loyal.
sentences.zh: 但其中有个问题：这些 condottieri 并不怎么忠诚。

sentences.en: If one city-state offered them a better deal, they might abandon their current employer—or worse, turn against them.
sentences.zh: 如果一个城邦提供更好的条件，他们可能会抛弃现有的雇主——或者更糟，调转枪头对付他们。

sentences.en: One example of this was a man called Francesco Sforza, who was one of the most famous condottieri of the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 其中的一个例子是一个叫弗朗切斯科·斯福尔扎（Francesco Sforza）的人，他是15世纪最著名的 condottieri 之一。

sentences.en: In the 1440s, Sforza was hired by the city of Milan to defend it against its rivals.
sentences.zh: 在1440年代，斯福尔扎被米兰城雇佣来保卫其免受竞争对手的侵害。

sentences.en: But rather than simply doing his job, Sforza saw an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但斯福尔扎没有简单地完成工作，而是看到了一个机会。

sentences.en: He betrayed Milan’s rulers, used his mercenary army to seize control of the city, and declared himself Duke of Milan.
sentences.zh: 他背叛了米兰的统治者，利用他的雇佣兵军队夺取了该城的控制权，并宣布自己为米兰公爵。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, for the condottieri, their primary driver was maximising their profit.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，对于 condottieri 来说，他们的首要驱动力是最大化利润。

sentences.en: So, unlike modern armies, the condottieri didn’t necessarily aim to win battles quickly or decisively.
sentences.zh: 因此，与现代军队不同，condottieri 不一定旨在迅速或决定性地赢得战斗。

sentences.en: There was little advantage to be had in slaughtering your enemy and completely eliminating the threat, as is often the goal in modern combat scenarios.
sentences.zh: 屠杀敌人并彻底消灭威胁并没有什么太大好处，正如这通常是现代作战场景中的目标一样。

sentences.en: Doing this could well mean that you would be out of your job, because your master might well say, “ok then, great job, you can go now, your services are no longer required”.
sentences.zh: 这样做很可能意味着你将失业，因为你的主子很可能会说：“好吧，干得好，你可以走了，不再需要你的服务了。”

sentences.en: So, many of them preferred to drag out conflicts because it meant longer contracts and more money.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们中的许多人更愿意拖延冲突，因为这意味着更长的合同和更多的钱。

sentences.en: And battles were often avoided altogether.
sentences.zh: 而且战斗往往完全可以避免。

sentences.en: Instead, the condottieri would rely on sieges, ambushes, and psychological tactics to wear down their opponents.
sentences.zh: 相反，condottieri 会依靠围城、伏击和心理战术来消耗对手。

sentences.en: This style of warfare was pragmatic and cost-effective for the mercenaries but often frustrating for the rulers who hired them.
sentences.zh: 这种战争风格对雇佣兵来说是务实且划算的，但对雇佣他们的统治者来说往往令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And when there were battles, they often weren’t battles as you might think of them.
sentences.zh: 当发生战斗时，它们往往也不是你想象的那种战斗。

sentences.en: One famous example of this came from a place called Anghiari.
sentences.zh: 一个著名的例子来自一个叫做安吉亚里（Anghiari）的地方。

sentences.en: Anghiari is a wonderful Tuscan hill town, but it is a sleepy place: there are more residents who are over the age of 75 than are under 18, and not an awful lot happens there.
sentences.zh: 安吉亚里是一个迷人的托斯卡纳山城，但它是一个安静的地方：75岁以上的居民比18岁以下的还要多，而且那里发生不了多少大事。

sentences.en: It is perhaps most famous for The Battle of Anghiari, which took place in 1440.
sentences.zh: 它或许最因发生于1440年的安吉亚里战役而闻名。

sentences.en: It was fought between forces loyal to the Duchy of Milan, and a consortium of fighters loyal to Florence, The Papal States, and Venice.
sentences.zh: 交战双方是效忠于米兰公国的军队，以及效忠于佛罗伦萨、教皇国和威尼斯的战士联盟。

sentences.en: The battle involved thousands of soldiers, lasted an entire day, and was commemorated in a painting by Leonardo Da Vinci, in which fearsome warriors tussle with each other on top of magnificent horses.
sentences.zh: 这场战役有数千名士兵参加，持续了一整天，并被达芬奇（Leonardo Da Vinci）的一幅画作所纪念，画中可怕的勇士们在雄壮的骏马背上激烈厮杀。

sentences.en: The reality, though, is that there was about as much blood spilt in the Battle of Anghiari as there is on a typical day in Anghiari in 2025: none.
sentences.zh: 然而，现实情况是，安吉亚里战役中流的血，大概和2025年安吉亚里寻常一天的流血量一样多：零。

sentences.en: So the legend goes, despite the thousands of soldiers, there was only one death, and this was from someone who accidentally fell off their horse.
sentences.zh: 据传说，尽管有数千名士兵，但只有一人死亡，而且这是由于某人不小心从马背上摔了下来。

sentences.en: The battle was fought by condottieri, and they simply had little interest in killing each other.
sentences.zh: 这场战斗是由 condottieri 打的，他们对互相杀戮实在没有什么兴趣。

sentences.en: Everyone would be far better off if they pretended to fight a little, and they could return to their masters with a large invoice and the prospect of more work to come.
sentences.zh: 如果大家都假装打一会儿，然后带着一大笔账单和未来更多工作的希望回到各自的主子身边，那么对所有人来说都会好得多。

sentences.en: Now, this was an extreme example, but it is reflective of the often misalignment of interests between the mercenary and his master.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极端的例子，但它反映了雇佣兵与其主子之间往往利益不一致的情况。

sentences.en: And by the late 15th century, the golden age of the condottieri was coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 到15世纪末，condottieri 的黄金时代走向了尾声。

sentences.en: There were several reasons for this decline.
sentences.zh: 这种衰落有几个原因。

sentences.en: First, the rise of more centralised states, like France and Spain, this brought larger, more disciplined armies to Italy.
sentences.zh: 首先，像法国和西班牙这样更加中央集权国家的崛起，给意大利带来了规模更大、纪律更严明的军队。

sentences.en: These national armies didn’t rely on mercenaries—they had received better training, were loyal to the state and often more effective in battle.
sentences.zh: 这些国家军队不依赖雇佣兵——他们接受过更好的训练，效忠于国家，在战斗中通常也更有效率。

sentences.en: Second, the unpredictable and self-serving nature of the condottieri made them a liability.
sentences.zh: 其次，condottieri 不可预测且唯利是图的性质使他们成了一个包袱。

sentences.en: While they'd been useful in the fragmented world of Renaissance Italy, they were no match for the organised, professional forces that began to dominate European warfare.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们在四分五裂的文艺复兴时期意大利很有用，但他们根本无法与开始主导欧洲战争的有组织、职业化的军队相抗衡。

sentences.en: Finally, the development of new military technologies, such as firearms and cannons, this required specialised training and coordination—it was something that mercenary bands were not equipped to handle.
sentences.zh: 最后，军事新技术的发展，例如火器和大炮，这需要专门的训练和协调——这是雇佣兵团无法应付的。

sentences.en: Now, despite their decline, the condottieri left a lasting mark on the history of warfare.
sentences.zh: 尽管走向衰落，condottieri 仍在战争史上留下了深刻的印记。

sentences.en: They were some of the first to formalise the idea of a professional fighting force, complete with contracts and structured payment systems.
sentences.zh: 他们是最早将职业化作战力量的概念规范化的人之一，配有合同和结构化的支付系统。

sentences.en: Now, for our second mercenary group, we are going to move forward almost to the present day.
sentences.zh: 现在，对于我们的第二组雇佣兵，我们将向前迈进，几乎来到当今时代。

sentences.en: Our next stop takes us to the late 20th and early 21st centuries, where we find a new type of mercenary emerging—not roaming soldiers with lances, but organised, corporate entities offering military services for profit.
sentences.zh: 我们的下一站将我们带到20世纪末和21世纪初，我们发现了一种新型雇佣兵的崛起——不再是带着长矛游荡的士兵，而是提供营利性军事服务的有组织的企业实体。

sentences.en: Among these, one name stands out: Blackwater.
sentences.zh: 其中，有一个名字格外引人注目：黑水公司（Blackwater）。

sentences.en: Blackwater was founded in 1997 by a man named Erik Prince, a former U.S.
sentences.zh: 黑水公司于1997年由一个名叫埃里克·普林斯（Erik Prince）的人创立，他曾是一名美国海豹突击队员。

sentences.en: Navy SEAL. He had spent two years in the SEALs before dropping out to start a company that he initially thought would focus on training for special operations.
sentences.zh: 他在海豹突击队待了两年，随后退役，开始创办一家他最初认为将专注于特种作战培训的公司。

sentences.en: Helped in no small part by the fact that his father sold a company for over a billion dollars, the young Prince bought 24 square kilometres of swampland in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 在他的父亲以超过十亿美元的价格卖掉了一家公司这一事实的很大帮助下，年轻的普林斯在北卡罗来纳州买下了24平方公里的沼泽地。

sentences.en: The idea was simple: he had this massive swathe of land, and his company would train law enforcement officers in key special operations techniques.
sentences.zh: 这个想法很简单：他拥有这片广袤的土地，他的公司将培训执法人员掌握关键的特种作战技术。

sentences.en: And initially, this is what Blackwater did.
sentences.zh: 最初，黑水公司做的就是这些。

sentences.en: But in the aftermath of the September 11th attacks in 2001, Blackwater’s business transformed almost overnight.
sentences.zh: 但在2001年“9·11”恐怖袭击之后，黑水公司的业务几乎在一夜之间转型。

sentences.en: The wars in Afghanistan and Iraq created an enormous demand for private contractors, and Blackwater was quick to position itself as a key player.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗战争和伊拉克战争产生了对私人承包商的巨大需求，黑水公司迅速把自己定位为关键参与者。

sentences.en: The company didn’t just provide training anymore.
sentences.zh: 这家公司不再仅仅提供培训。

sentences.en: It started offering security services, logistical support, and even armed combat capabilities.
sentences.zh: 它开始提供安保服务、后勤支持，甚至武装战斗能力。

sentences.en: Soldiers, essentially.
sentences.zh: 说白了，就是士兵。

sentences.en: At the height of the Iraq War, Blackwater became one of the most prominent private military companies in the world, securing lucrative contracts from the U.S. government.
sentences.zh: 在伊拉克战争最激烈的时候，黑水公司成为世界上最著名的私人军事公司之一，从美国政府那里拿到了利润丰厚的合同。

sentences.en: At one point, it was reported that Blackwater personnel outnumbered American troops in some regions of Iraq.
sentences.zh: 据报道，在伊拉克某些地区，黑水公司人员的数量一度超过了美军。

sentences.en: This was a new kind of mercenary force—corporate, professional, and deeply tied to modern warfare’s complex logistics.
sentences.zh: 这是一种新型的雇佣兵力量——企业化、专业化，并且深深嵌入到现代战争复杂的后勤中。

sentences.en: However, with this rise to prominence came controversy.
sentences.zh: 然而，伴随着这种名声鹊起而来的是争议。

sentences.en: In 2007, Blackwater contractors were involved in an incident that became infamous: the Nisour Square massacre in Baghdad.
sentences.zh: 2007年，黑水公司的承包商卷入了一起臭名昭著的事件：巴格达尼苏尔广场屠杀事件（Nisour Square massacre）。

sentences.en: During a security mission, Blackwater guards opened fire on a crowded intersection, killing 17 Iraqi civilians and injuring many more.
sentences.zh: 在一次安保任务中，黑水公司的警卫向一个拥挤的十字路口开枪，造成17名伊拉克平民死亡，多人受伤。

sentences.en: The event sparked international outrage and led to accusations that private contractors like Blackwater lacked the accountability of regular armed forces, operated with impunity, and existed outside the bounds of military law.
sentences.zh: 这一事件引发了国际社会的愤怒，并导致人们指责像黑水公司这样的私人承包商缺乏正规武装力量所具有的问责制，肆意妄为，游离于军事法律的约束之外。

sentences.en: And this is an interesting point. Mercenaries are considered differently from ordinary soldiers when it comes to international law.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的点。在国际法方面，雇佣兵与普通士兵的待遇不同。

sentences.en: Under the Geneva Convention, they are not considered lawful combatants, so they don’t receive the same protections.
sentences.zh: 根据《日内瓦公约》，他们不被认为是合法的战斗人员，因此无法获得相同的保护。

sentences.en: Now, there are all sorts of loopholes here about who is and who isn’t a mercenary, and the definition isn’t always so clear.
sentences.zh: 这里面存在各种各样的漏洞，关于谁是、谁不是雇佣兵，其定义并不总是那么清晰。

sentences.en: To give you an example, let’s just take the same person.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我们就拿同一个人来说。

sentences.en: Bill is a United States citizen. He signs up for the regular army, he receives a salary, and he is sent to war.
sentences.zh: 比尔（Bill）是美国公民。他报名参加了正规军，领薪水，然后被派往战场。

sentences.en: Bill is a regular soldier, not a mercenary.
sentences.zh: 比尔是一名正规士兵，而不是雇佣兵。

sentences.en: But let’s say that Bill leaves the regular army and joins a company like Blackwater.
sentences.zh: 但假设比尔离开了正规军，加入了一家像黑水公司这样的公司。

sentences.en: He still receives a salary, and he is sent to war, or probably more accurately, he is “sent to provide security services in a warzone”.
sentences.zh: 他依然领着薪水，被派往战场，或者可能更准确地说，他被“派往战区提供安保服务”。

sentences.en: It’s still the same Bill, he is still in the same place, fighting for the same United States.
sentences.zh: 他依然是那个比尔，依然在同一个地方，为同一个美国作战。

sentences.en: Is he now a mercenary just because his contract is with a private company rather than with the United States government?
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为他的合同是与一家私人公司签订的，而不是与美国政府签订的，他现在就是雇佣兵了吗？

sentences.en: And therefore, should he be treated differently when it comes to international law?
sentences.zh: 因此，在涉及国际法时，他应该受到不同的对待吗？

sentences.en: As you can see, the lines aren’t always so clear.
sentences.zh: 正如你所看到的，界限并不总是那么清晰。

sentences.en: But back to Blackwater. After the controversy of the Nisour Square massacre, and growing criticism about how much money it was making from the US government, it rebranded itself several times and has been sold and repackaged on numerous occasions.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，回到黑水公司。在尼苏尔广场屠杀事件的争议以及对其从美国政府赚取巨额资金的日益批评之后，它多次更改品牌，并在许多场合被出售和重新包装。

sentences.en: Today, it operates as part of a holding group called Constellis, and it is perhaps the most prominent example of the privatisation and commercialisation of war.
sentences.zh: 今天，它作为一家名为康斯特利斯（Constellis）的控股集团的一部分运营，它或许是战争私有化和商业化最突出的例子。

sentences.en: But Blackwater is far from the only example of modern mercenaries, or Private Military Contractors, PMCs for short.
sentences.zh: 但黑水公司远非现代雇佣兵或私人军事承包商（简称 PMC）的唯一例子。

sentences.en: Our final stop takes us to the modern-day and one of the most controversial mercenary groups in the world: the Wagner Group.
sentences.zh: 我们的最后一站将我们带到当今时代，以及世界上最具争议的雇佣兵集团之一：瓦格纳集团（Wagner Group）。

sentences.en: If Blackwater represented the corporate face of modern mercenaries, Wagner is something altogether different—a shadowy organisation that blends private military operations with state interests, operating in a legal and ethical grey zone.
sentences.zh: 如果说黑水公司代表了现代雇佣兵的企业面孔，那么瓦格纳则完全是另一回事——一个将私人军事行动与国家利益融合在一起的暗影组织，游走于法律和道德的灰色地带。

sentences.en: The Wagner Group emerged in 2014 during Russia’s annexation of Crimea and the conflict in Eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳集团于2014年俄罗斯吞并克里米亚以及乌克兰东部冲突期间浮出水面。

sentences.en: It was founded by a man named Yevgeny Prigozhin, a businessman with close ties to Vladimir Putin, and Dmitry Utkin, a former officer in Russia’s military intelligence service.
sentences.zh: 它由一个名叫叶夫根尼·普里戈津（Yevgeny Prigozhin）的人创立，他是一名与弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）关系密切的商人，另一位创始人德米特里·乌特金（Dmitry Utkin）则是俄罗斯军方情报部门的前军官。

sentences.en: Officially, Wagner is a private military company, a PMC, but in practice, it operates as an unofficial arm of the Russian government, carrying out missions that Moscow cannot officially acknowledge.
sentences.zh: 官方上，瓦格纳是一家私人军事公司，即 PMC，但在实践中，它作为俄罗斯政府的非官方分支机构运作，执行莫斯科官方无法承认的任务。

sentences.en: It first gained international attention for its role in Ukraine, where its fighters were involved in key battles in the Donbas region.
sentences.zh: 它因在乌克兰的角色而首次获得国际关注，其武装人员参与了顿巴斯地区的关键战役。

sentences.en: These mercenaries were well-equipped and well-trained.
sentences.zh: 这些雇佣兵装备精良，训练有素。

sentences.en: They were often recruited from Russian special forces or veterans of elite military units.
sentences.zh: 他们通常从俄罗斯特种部队或精锐军事单位的退伍军人中招募。

sentences.en: Unlike regular soldiers, Wagner’s troops operated with plausible deniability, allowing Russia to maintain a degree of separation from their actions.
sentences.zh: 与正规军不同，瓦格纳的部队以“合理否认”的方式行动，使俄罗斯能够与其行动保持一定程度的距离。

sentences.en: The use of Wagner troops also meant that Putin could delay his partial mobilisation, the calling up of reservist troops from the general population, and thus continue his claim that this was not a war that would affect the regular Russian population.
sentences.zh: 使用瓦格纳部队还意味着普京可以推迟他的部分动员令——即从普通民众中征召预备役部队，从而继续坚称这不是一场会影响普通俄罗斯民众的战争。

sentences.en: As you may know, that didn’t last particularly long, just 7 months after the invasion.
sentences.zh: 你可能也知道，那并没有持续太久，就在入侵后仅仅7个月。

sentences.en: But Wagner’s activities extend far beyond Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 但瓦格纳的活动远远超出了乌克兰。

sentences.en: The group has been involved in conflicts across the Middle East and Africa, often aligning itself with regimes that Russia seeks to support.
sentences.zh: 该集团一直卷入中东和非洲的冲突，经常与俄罗斯试图支持的政权结盟。

sentences.en: In Syria, Wagner fought alongside forces loyal to President Bashar al-Assad, securing oil fields and other strategic assets.
sentences.zh: 在叙利亚，瓦格纳与效忠于巴沙尔·阿萨德（Bashar al-Assad）总统的部队并肩作战，保卫油田和其他战略资产。

sentences.en: In Africa, Wagner has operated in countries like Libya, Sudan, and the Central African Republic, providing security for unstable governments in exchange for access to valuable resources such as gold and diamonds.
sentences.zh: 在非洲，瓦格纳在利比亚、苏丹和中非共和国等国家活动，向不稳定的政府提供安保，以换取获得黄金和钻石等宝贵资源的途径。

sentences.en: And while Wagner’s fighters are technically “private contractors,” their close ties to the Kremlin make them much more than just a mercenary force.
sentences.zh: 虽然瓦格纳的战士在技术上是“私人承包商”，但他们与克里姆林宫的紧密联系使他们远不止是一支雇佣兵力量。

sentences.en: They function as a tool of Russian foreign policy, extending Moscow’s influence in regions where it has strategic or economic interests.
sentences.zh: 他们充当俄罗斯外交政策的工具，在莫斯科拥有战略或经济利益的地区扩大其影响力。

sentences.en: This dual role—as both a profit-driven organisation and a geopolitical instrument—sets Wagner apart from other PMCs like Blackwater.
sentences.zh: 这种双重角色——既是营利性组织又是地缘政治工具——使瓦格纳区别于黑水公司等其他 PMC。

sentences.en: But it is not the only difference. The level of violence Wagner seems prepared to use puts it in another category altogether.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是唯一的区别。瓦格纳准备使用的暴力程度将其置于完全不同的类别中。

sentences.en: Yes, Blackwater contractors clearly did awful things in Iraq, but the ongoing conduct of Wagner soldiers is in another league.
sentences.zh: 是的，黑水公司的承包商在伊拉克显然做过可怕的事情，但瓦格纳士兵一贯的行为完全是另一个级别的。

sentences.en: The group has been accused of committing war crimes, including targeting civilians, extrajudicial killings, and torture.
sentences.zh: 该集团被指控犯下战争罪，包括针对平民、法外处决和酷刑。

sentences.en: One of the most infamous incidents involves a video of Wagner operatives allegedly using a sledgehammer to execute a Syrian prisoner.
sentences.zh: 其中最臭名昭著的事件涉及一段视频，内容据称是瓦格纳特工使用大锤处决一名叙利亚囚犯。

sentences.en: It is grim stuff, indeed. And while it might have been more distant, at an arm’s length from the Russian state, Wagner is reportedly now even more closely tied to the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 这确实是残酷的勾当。虽然过去它可能更遥远，与俄罗斯国家保持着一定距离，但据报道，现在瓦格纳与克里姆林宫的联系甚至更加紧密。

sentences.en: As you may remember, in June 2023, the leader of the Wagner Group, Yevgeny Prigozhin, launched a rebellion and marched towards Moscow, before backing down and apparently solving his issues with Putin.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，在2023年6月，瓦格纳集团领导人叶夫根尼·普里戈津发动了一场叛乱并向莫斯科进发，随后退缩，显然解决了与普京的问题。

sentences.en: Clearly, these issues were not solved, as Prigozhin died in a plane crash a few months later, and what this has meant, according to many Russia watchers, is that Wagner has more closely integrated with the regular Russian forces.
sentences.zh: 显然，这些问题并没有解决，因为普里戈津几个月后在一次坠机事故中身亡，据许多俄罗斯问题观察家称，这意味着瓦格纳已经更紧密地融入了俄罗斯正规军。

sentences.en: They are still in Ukraine, they are still in Africa, they are still in the Middle East, and still often operate in this grey zone: part Private Military Company, part state actor, and able to shift between the two when the need arises.
sentences.zh: 他们仍在乌克兰，仍在非洲，仍在中东，并且仍然经常在这个灰色地带运作：部分是私人军事公司，部分是国家行为体，能够在需要时在两者之间切换。

sentences.en: Now, to wrap things up, from Renaissance Italy to modern paramilitaries, one thing is clear: the idea of soldiers for hire is anything but new.
sentences.zh: 好了，总结一下，从文艺复兴时期的意大利到现代准军事组织，有一件事是清晰的：雇佣兵的观念一点也不新鲜。

sentences.en: Money, as they say, talks—and it speaks loudly on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 正如人们所说，金钱会说话——它在战场上声音洪亮。

sentences.en: Renaissance condottieri, corporate PMCs, and modern-day groups like Wagner all show us different faces of the same truth: war, for some, is just another business.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴时期的 condottieri、企业 PMC 以及像瓦格纳这样的现代集团，都向我们展示了同一个真理的不同面孔：对某些人来说，战争只是又一笔生意。

sentences.en: As long as there is money to be made, there will always be someone willing to fight.
sentences.zh: 只要有利可图，就总会有人愿意去战斗。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是今天关于雇佣兵的全部内容。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 我希望这期节目很有趣，并且你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目有什么看法。

sentences.en: Are there any linguistic influences from the world of mercenaries that have entered your language?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么来自雇佣兵世界的语言影响已经进入了你的语言？

sentences.en: How do you think mercenaries should be treated in the eyes of the law?
sentences.zh: 你认为在法律眼中应该如何对待雇佣兵？

sentences.en: I would love to know, so let’s get this discussion started.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，所以让我们开始讨论吧。

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的人交流畅谈。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目见。
